title: Starlake Private Connectivity & Interconnect Onramp - Discovery
summary: Initial discovery to understand Starlake's private onramp requirements for Redwood Private: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints (EU/NA), egress controls, KMS integration, and pilot timeline. Agreed to share network diagram, security whitepaper and schedule technical deep dive for transit gateway configuration and a small benchmark run in GA-East region.
topics: KMS/HSM key management and encryption at rest
action_items: Maya Chen: Share Redwood Private network_onramp_diagram.pdf and SOC2 pack (due 2027-02-17)
Diego Alvarez: Schedule technical deep dive for transit gateway setup and IP addressing plan (due 2027-02-19)
Daniel Park: Provide current VPC CIDR ranges, NAT/egress appliance details, and approved peering account IDs (due 2027-02-18)
next_steps: Redwood to send security artifacts and standard network diagrams
Schedule SE-led deep dive to walk through Transit Gateway and PrivateLink options
Agree on pilot region (eu-west-1 or us-east-1) and window for a 1-week benchmark
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Starlake Platform), Liam O'Neill (Starlake Security), Daniel Park (Cloud Architect), Sofia Martins (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Starlake is evaluating Redwood Private for latency-sensitive inference that must stay inside EU and NA. Key constraints: no internet egress for inference traffic, KMS integration, and centralized egress inspection via a firewall appliance. They are leaning toward private endpoints but want options for Transit Gateway peering if scale or cross-region routing becomes necessary.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate the time. quick run through agenda — connectivity options, regions, security requirements, and next steps. you mentioned a couple hard constraints in the intake form, priya, want to confirm those up front?
00:28 Priya: yeah thanks maya. the big ones are, one, we need inference traffic to stay in our VPCs, two, no model payloads can traverse the public internet, three, EU data residency for eu customers, and four, we need KMS integration for keys. we also have an internal egress inspection appliance we want to route through.
01:05 Diego: got it. so two high-level patterns we typically propose: Private Endpoints (PrivateLink-style) which give you per-region private connectivity, or Transit Gateway / peering which is useful if you want broad, low-latency cross-account routing. both support KMS integration on Redwood Private, but the network flows differ.
01:40 Liam: how do you handle egress? i.e., our IDS and firewall must see outbound calls for compliance. can we force all outbound from the Redwood nodes back to our NAC?
02:15 Diego: yes, you can route egress back to your NAT/egress appliance by advertising routes for the Redwood subnet and setting the next-hop. in PrivateLink mode, you still get private IPs and you can control egress via your route table. with TGW there's more flexibility for central inspection across many VPCs.
02:50 Priya: ok, we run across two regions primarily — eu-west-1 and us-east-1 — and for eu we cannot leave eu region for those customer models. how strict is Redwood about regional model placement?
03:20 Maya: we support per-region model pinning for Redwood Private. you can pin specific model versions to eu-west-1 only. if you want multi-region active-active, we can do that but by default you can keep workloads regional to satisfy residency.
03:55 Daniel: what's the IP allocation like? we need to avoid CIDR overlap with our service VPCs. do you support secondary CIDR and flexible ranges?
04:25 Diego: yes, when you deploy Redwood Private you propose a VPC/subnet plan. we prefer you allocate a /20 or /19 depending on scale — nodes, KV cache, load balancers. we can use non-overlapping ranges and we support bringing your own IPs (BYOIP) in peered setups.
05:00 Sofia: one of our concerns is cross-account permissions. our security team will not accept broad peering, they want least privilege and clear ownership. how do you handle access and audit logs?
05:35 Maya: Redwood Private integrates with your SSO (SAML/SCIM) for RBAC, and our control plane can be deployed in your account or as a customer-managed control plane so audit logs stay in your environment. we also provide per-request logging hooks and long-term export to your SIEM via Kinesis/Logstash.
06:10 Liam: SOC2, ISO, that sort of thing — we need to see the reports before we move forward.
06:35 Maya: absolutely. i'll send the SOC2 type 2 pack and our architecture whitepaper after the call.
07:00 Diego: one nuance — if you route through an egress appliance that does TLS interception, we need to coordinate certs for our control plane and data plane comms. normally we recommend TLS passthrough for model traffic, but many customers place an inspection appliance in the path.
07:35 Priya: our appliance does TLS inspection on outbound flows, yes. for private traffic we can exempt certain destination CNs, but we'd prefer minimal exceptions. is there a way to have mTLS between Redwood nodes and your endpoints so inspection can't break encryption and yet our appliance can still validate?
08:08 Diego: mTLS is supported on the control plane. For the inference node-to-node model traffic, we support mutual TLS for management channels; payloads are encrypted at rest and in transit. If your appliance can't intercept without breaking policy, we can provide flow logs and extended metadata to your SIEM instead of full interception.
08:45 Daniel: another operational question: how do you handle upgrades, rollouts, and fallback? we can't risk a bad rollout touching our production inference.
09:10 Maya: we do canary rollouts by default; with Redwood Dedicated/Private you can pin model versions and roll out on a per-route basis. if you want absolute isolation during pilot we can deploy a dedicated pool for your account so rollouts won't affect other tenants.
09:40 Liam: pricing question — if we take a private deployment with dedicated pools and transit gateway peering, how different is cost vs hosted?
10:10 Maya: dedicated pools carry an infra commitment; network egress savings vary. compared to hosted, you'll pay for reserved capacity and networking (TGW/transit attachments). we can run a cost estimate once we have footprint numbers.
10:40 Priya: about private endpoints — what's the latency overhead vs peering? we care about sub-10ms for some workloads in eu-west-1.
11:05 Diego: PrivateLink-style endpoints usually add fewer network hops inside the region and tend to be slightly lower latency for single-VPC calls. TGW is great for hub-and-spoke but can add hairpinning depending on route tables. For strict sub-10ms SLOs, we generally recommend colocating model pools in the same AZ or region and using private endpoints.
11:45 Sofia: do you support colocated private endpoints per-AZ? some teams want even AZ-local endpoints to avoid cross-AZ charges and latency variance.
12:10 Diego: we can deploy multi-AZ nodes and private endpoints in each AZ. we recommend measuring at pilot scale to confirm the variance.
12:40 Daniel: are there any special firewall ports we need to open or static IPs to whitelist?
13:05 Diego: we'll provide a small set of CIDR ranges for control plane and data plane. For PrivateLink the destination is your VPC endpoint, so less whitelisting. For outbound egress to external KMS or monitoring endpoints, you'll need to allow our control plane IPs or integrate over VPC endpoints for those services as well.
13:40 Liam: KMS — do you integrate with customer-managed keys in AWS KMS or external HSM?
14:05 Maya: yes, we support customer-managed KMS keys in AWS KMS and integrations with external HSMs via KMIP where supported. keys can be used for encrypting model artifacts at rest; access controls are granular.
14:40 Priya: whats the timeline — we're hoping to start a pilot in 6 weeks if everything looks good.
15:05 Maya: that seems doable. typical pilot path: (1) exchange network diagrams and agree on CIDR/IPs, (2) SE deep dive to design TGW or PrivateLink, (3) limited deployment in selected region for a week of benchmarks, (4) review results and expand.
15:40 Diego: for the SE deep dive i'd like to get your VPC ranges and a quick topo diagram. daniel, can you send that after the call?
16:05 Daniel: i'll export the VPC ranges and current TGW attachments; expect that by tomorrow.
16:30 Sofia: a question on logging — if we keep the control plane in our account, do you still provide Redwood console?
16:55 Maya: yes, we can surface telemetry in Redwood Console; when control plane is customer-managed we provide a console-facing portal with read-only links or we can push metrics into your own observability stack.
17:20 Priya: any constraints around region support — for eu we need everything inside eu-west-1, but we also want low-latency support for na-east region for US customers. do you support deploying separate Private clusters per-region?
17:50 Diego: absolutely. private clusters can be deployed per-region and you can pin models regionally. we do suggest separate control plane instances if you need strong separation, otherwise you can use a single control plane with region-scoped model pins.
18:20 Liam: about compliance — do you provide access to raw audit logs for e-discovery?
18:45 Maya: yes, audit logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM; retention and export policies are configurable by customer.
19:05 Priya: our legal team will want to know about data deletion guarantees. if we delete a model or data, how quickly is it purged from backups?
19:30 Diego: we have configurable retention windows; for strict deletion policies we can shorten backups and do immediate re-encryption or key revocation patterns. we'll include the deletion guarantees in the security pack.
20:00 Daniel: network peering acceptance process — we have a security review that typically takes 2 weeks, and we might require a separate VPC for vendors. is it possible to do a trial in a vendor VPC with restricted access?
20:30 Maya: yes, many customers start in a vendor VPC or pilot account. Redwood Private supports both customer-managed and vendor-managed deployments; we'll note the constraints for your security review.
21:00 Sofia: curious about bursting — if we use dedicated pools but need to spike, do you support temporary burst capacity without changing routes?
21:30 Maya: yes, there's a burst option. we can allow spillover to compatible hosted capacity with customer consent. for private-only traffic you can configure an on-failure fallback policy to mapped model variants within your private footprint.
22:05 Priya: what's the minimum footprint for a pilot? we want meaningful latency numbers but not full production cost.
22:30 Diego: typically a 2-3 node pool per-region is enough to get representative latency and throughput numbers for small pilots. we'll size based on your qps targets.
23:00 Liam: let's talk about how we prove data never leaves region — can you provide network traces or pcap-style evidence?
23:35 Diego: we can provide flow logs and trace-level telemetry. in prior engagements we produced per-request metadata that shows the region and VPC path; full packet captures we don't typically provide but flow logs + TLS cert verification and routing snapshots are usually sufficient for audits.
24:10 Priya: ok. another thing — we use an internal identity provider with SAML; does Redwood SCIM support on-prem SCIM endpoints?
24:40 Maya: we support SAML for SSO and SCIM provisioning for many IdPs. if your IdP is on-prem, we have integrations and can offer a connector pattern using a small agent or outbound SAML assertions. we'll capture your vendor in the follow-up.
25:10 Daniel: are there known gotchas for cross-account TGW attachments — e.g., asymmetric routing or SNAT requirements?
25:40 Diego: yes, asymmetric routing can occur if you have overlapping CIDRs or multiple TGW attachments. we recommend central route tables and careful CIDR planning. SNAT is sometimes required for egress appliances; we'll document recommended NAT behavior in the design doc.
26:15 Sofia: what about provider-level rate limiting — will Redwood throttle our calls and how do we surface that to ops?
26:45 Maya: we expose per-token and per-route metrics in the console and allow you to set soft and hard rate limits. if throttling happens we emit events and traces you can forward to your pager.
27:20 Priya: fine. i want to highlight a policy: no third-party data plane in APAC for now. we won't accept data going through any APAC region due to clients. does Redwood have any hidden cross-region fallbacks?
27:55 Diego: there are no hidden fallbacks. any automatic failover to another region only happens if you configure cross-region redundancy and enable fallback. we never route traffic to APAC unless configured.
28:30 Liam: can we get a written statement for that to include in the compliance packet?
28:55 Maya: yes, we'll include an explicit regional routing statement.
29:20 Daniel: i'd like to get more concrete about IPs — will you provide static egress IPs or ranges for us to allowlist?
29:45 Diego: we provide ranges. for PrivateLink the destination is inside your VPC so no external allowlist is needed. for control plane callbacks or metrics endpoints we provide a small set of IP ranges.
30:15 Sofia: one more on monitoring — can we push Prometheus metrics or do we have to pull from Redwood?
30:40 Maya: we can push metrics into your Prometheus/Grafana via remote write or we can expose scraping endpoints inside your network. we'll tailor based on your preference.
31:05 Priya: ok. at this point, can we sketch out a pilot milestone plan?
31:30 Maya: sure. week 0-1: exchange diagrams and sign network NDA if needed; week 2: deploy pilot infra in chosen region; week 3: run benchmarks and collect metrics; week 4: review and plan expansion.
32:00 Daniel: what about support — SRE on-call during pilot?
32:25 Maya: we provide SE on-call coverage during pilot windows and a response SLA for critical incidents. we'll include contact info in the follow-up calendar invite.
32:55 Diego: from an SE perspective i'd like to run a low-level routing diagram with your network team. can we set 60-90 minutes for that deep dive?
33:20 Daniel: yes, 90 minutes would be good. preferably early next week.
33:45 Priya: our earliest window is tuesday morning eu time.
34:05 Maya: i'll propose times after the call.
34:30 Liam: one quick security ask: will Redwood allow us to rotate KMS keys on our schedule without breaking model access?
34:55 Diego: yes, we support key rotation; you can rotate keys but you'll need to coordinate re-encryption windows. we recommend a key-rotation runbook, and we'll help validate the process during pilot.
35:25 Sofia: any additional licensing for HSM-backed keys?
35:50 Maya: HSM integrations may have additional fees depending on the provider, and the enterprise support tier covers HSM configuration. we'll detail costs in the follow-up.
36:20 Daniel: curious about encryption in transit for internal metrics streams — are those encrypted end-to-end?
36:45 Diego: metrics can be sent over mTLS and are encrypted. control plane and data plane communicate over mutual TLS with cert pinning if you're using customer-managed control plane.
37:15 Priya: ok great. i'm going to summarize: you will send SOC2, whitepaper, network_onramp_diagram.pdf, and proposed IP ranges. we will send VPC CIDRs, TGW attachments, and a list of appliances. next step is SE deep dive. does that capture it?
37:50 Maya: yes that's perfect. any other outstanding questions?
38:10 Liam: one last thing — are you able to provide a short bench script we can run client-side to measure P99 and p50 latencies against the private endpoints?
38:35 Diego: yes, we have a simple benchmark harness that simulates token streaming and end-to-end latency. we'll share the repo link and instructions.
39:00 Priya: great. i'm also going to loop legal in after we get SOC2.
39:25 Daniel: note, our security review will probably ask for packet-level evidence; earlier you said flow logs are usually enough. can you include an example report?
39:50 Maya: we'll include a sample flow log export and a sample trace report.
40:15 Sofia: are there any known limitations with CloudFormation or Terraform modules for setting up endpoints?
40:40 Diego: we provide Terraform modules and CloudFormation templates for endpoint creation, TGW attachments, and route tables. we'll share those in the repo.
41:05 Priya: timing on that repo?
41:25 Diego: i'll drop links in the follow-up email — usually within 24 hours.
41:45 Maya: anything else? if not, thanks all — we'll follow up with artifacts and set the SE deep dive.
42:05 Liam: thanks, appreciated.
42:20 Daniel: thanks everyone.
42:35 Priya: bye.
